title: AI-Powered Banking Cybersecurity Intelligence System
businessProblem: A tier-1 commercial retail bank faces multi-vector cyber threats: advanced credential stuffing attacks, targeted spear-phishing campaigns against executive officers, lateral malware movements bypassing traditional antivirus, and fraudulent unauthorized cross-border wire transfers totaling $22M in annual risk.

unitMapping.roleInSolution: Unit I (Foundations): Telemetry ingestion from core banking gateways, Kafka log bus, feature normalization, and handling extreme label scarcity.
Unit II (Arsenal): Unsupervised Isolation Forest and GBDT algorithms analyzing internal network flows for stealthy lateral intrusion.
Unit III (Threat Detection): Transformer NLP email gateway scanning inbound messages for Business Email Compromise (BEC) and homoglyph domain fraud.
Unit IV (Protection & Auth): Continuous behavioral biometrics (keystroke flight times, mouse acceleration) guarding customer web banking sessions.
Unit V (Fraud Prevention): Sub-25ms LightGBM ensemble scoring transactions with cost-sensitive weighting to block unauthorized fund movement.

inputData:
1. Inbound corporate email MIME payloads with SPF/DKIM headers.
2. Core banking transaction events: { card_id, amount, merchant_category, timestamp, geo_coordinates }.
3. NetFlow telemetry (VPC flows, TCP flags, packet size distributions, byte entropy).
4. Web session sensor metrics (keystroke dwell times, flight times, mobile device gyroscope jitter).
stepByStepProcess: Step 1: Ingestion & Feature Store - Event streams flow via Apache Kafka into a unified streaming feature store (Feast/Redis).
Step 2: Boundary Filtration - Known malicious IOCs (IPs, hashes) dropped immediately by deterministic firewalls to conserve compute.
Step 3: Perimeter Threat Scanning - Email classifier (RoBERTa) scores inbound messages for urgency and brand deception, auto-quarantining phishing lures.
Step 4: Continuous Behavioral Authentication - Customer web and mobile sessions continuously scored via behavioral biometric models, prompting step-up MFA if flight-time variance spikes.
Step 5: Core Network Anomaly Detection - Unsupervised Isolation Forests analyze internal server-to-server traffic to detect anomalous lateral movement or credential harvesting.
Step 6: Real-Time Payment Decisioning - LightGBM fraud engine evaluates fund transfers within a 20ms SLA, declining fraudulent attempts and alerting the Security Operations Center (SOC).
expectedOutput:
1. Phishing Quarantine Decision (Confidence score 0.0 - 1.0).
2. Continuous Session Trust Score (Frictionless / Step-Up MFA / Session Termination).
3. Lateral Movement Alert with identified source host, target IP, and anomalous entropy metric.
4. Real-time Payment Authorization (ALLOW / REVIEW / DECLINE) with SHAP feature contribution explanation.
practicalApplication: Deployed in active production environments across 14 million active bank accounts, delivering a 78% reduction in successful account takeovers and preventing $18.4M in fraudulent transfers within the first operational quarter.
limitations: Requires continuous model retraining to prevent concept drift caused by evolving attacker evasion techniques.
High-throughput inference requires dedicated GPU/ASIC inference accelerators for transformer models.
Regulatory mandates (e.g. EU AI Act, RBI guidelines) require explainable AI (XAI) outputs such as SHAP or LIME for every declined transaction.
